sentence: This project builds a central data system that stores, checks and shares data and runs statistical analyses for the other projects.
This project studies how a transcription factor works in neurons and whether changing its activity could prevent cell death in Alzheimer's disease.
This project builds computer simulation methods to study how enzymes maintain, repair and modify DNA, and how the proteins involved work.
This project builds a tool for modeling changes made to proteins after they are made, to learn how these changes affect health and disease.
This project studies how changes in DNA methylation drive the activation of microglia, immune cells of the brain, in Alzheimer's disease.
This project grows small brain-like organoids from people with autism spectrum disorder to find out what causes their brains to overgrow early in life.
This project tries to find out how Salmonella gets past a nutritional defense that human immune cells use against intracellular pathogens.
This project studies how a signaling pathway involving neuropeptides affects escalated alcohol intake and the brain changes linked to alcohol use disorder.
This project builds a mobile health tool guided by an avatar for young adults who binge drink and have thoughts of suicide.
This project studies what controls whether intestinal stem cells are actively dividing or resting at different stages of development.
This project mines gene activity data from single cells to find which genes drive disease in people who have both HIV and substance use disorder.
This project builds very sensitive tools to measure how T cells release cytokines and to learn how the cell membrane controls this release.
This project studies why some lungs scar after injury while others heal normally, focusing on one protein in lung lining cells.
This project tests whether drugs that block the effects of adenosine could help the immune system attack chordoma tumor cells.
This project studies how groups of nerve cells that run down from the brain are used to produce movement and avoid collisions.
This project creates mouse and rat models and kidney organoids grown from stem cells for researchers who study polycystic kidney diseases.
This project uses gene activity readouts from single bacteria and phages to learn how infections work and to design phage therapies and antibiotics.
This project builds optical tools that use timing information to measure several fluorescent probes at once in a single microscope image.
This project studies how differences in the viral surface of mosquito-borne flaviviruses affect infection and how antibodies neutralize them.
This project builds botulinum proteases that can enter skin cells and stop neurons and immune cells from releasing signals that cause inflammation.
